from cache import make_key
from service import score

def test_cache_invalidation():
    store = {}
    compute_calls = []
    def compute():
        compute_calls.append(len(compute_calls))
        return f'val{len(compute_calls)}'
    
    # first call
    job_text = 'job'
    profile_version = 'v1'
    criteria_version = 'c1'
    res1 = score(store, job_text, profile_version, criteria_version, compute)
    assert res1 == 'val1'
    assert len(compute_calls) == 1
    
    # change job_text only
    res2 = score(store, 'job2', profile_version, criteria_version, compute)
    assert res2 == 'val2'
    assert len(compute_calls) == 2
    
    # change profile only
    res3 = score(store, job_text, 'v2', criteria_version, compute)
    assert res3 == 'val3'
    assert len(compute_calls) == 3
    
    # change criteria only
    res4 = score(store, job_text, profile_version, 'c2', compute)
    assert res4 == 'val4'
    assert len(compute_calls) == 4
    
    # change two inputs
    res5 = score(store, 'job2', 'v2', 'c2', compute)
    assert res5 == 'val5'
    assert len(compute_calls) == 5
    
    # reuse same inputs
    res6 = score(store, job_text, profile_version, criteria_version, compute)
    # should return cached val1, not recompute
    assert res6 == 'val1'
    # compute_calls should not increase
    assert len(compute_calls) == 5

def test_make_key():
    key = make_key('text', 'prof', 'criterion')
    # key should be tuple of three values
    assert key == ('text', 'prof', 'criterion')
    # different inputs produce different keys
    key2 = make_key('text', 'prof', 'criterion')
    assert key == key2
    key3 = make_key('text', 'prof', 'other')
    assert key != key3

if __name__ == '__main__':
    test_make_key()
    test_cache_invalidation()
    print('All tests passed')
